headline: KIRKLAND LAKE DISCOVERIES EXPANDS MIRADO NORTH ZONE 125M NW — 2.78 g/t Au Over 21.50m in Step-Out; Two New Holes Confirm Ontario System Growing
snippet: Kirkland Lake Discoveries (TSX-V: KLDC) reported two new step-out holes at the Mirado project in Ontario that extend the North Zone approximately 125 metres both northwest and vertically, with a headline intercept of 2.78 g/t Au over 21.50 metres. The result confirms the North Zone remains open and is growing in multiple directions simultaneously — an important distinction from many Ontario gold juniors whose 2026 programs stalled at or near historical limits. At Mirado's KL South location, 18 km from Kirkland Lake, the company has been drilling continuously since spring 2026 with encouraging continuity at depth.

headline: ONYX GOLD'S MAIDEN SE HOLE: 1.6 G/T AU OVER 24.8M — New Target Pushes Munro-Croesus Gold Trend to 4 km; Company's Largest Surface Footprint
snippet: Onyx Gold (TSX-V: ONYX) reported 1.6 g/t gold over 24.8 metres in the first hole drilled at a new southeast target at the Munro-Croesus project near Timmins, Ontario, extending the company's gold-bearing trend to approximately 4 kilometres — its largest demonstrated surface footprint to date. The intercept is from drill hole MC26-357, confirming that gold mineralization extends in a new direction beyond the well-defined Argus zone that the company has been systematically expanding throughout its 2026 program. A 4 km gold trend at Munro-Croesus positions Onyx as one of the more advanced bulk-tonnage junior stories in the Timmins camp.

headline: IMC RARE EARTHS HITS NEW TERBIUM AND YTTRIUM IN BLOCKS H AND D — Itarantim Brazil Returns Heavy REE Mineralization; H1 Cash Burn Modest at $3.5M
snippet: IMC Rare Earths (ASX/TSX) reported new terbium and yttrium mineralization from exploratory drilling at Blocks H and D at its Itarantim project in Bahia, Brazil, alongside half-year financial results showing $3.5 million in operating cash used over the six months ended September 30, 2026. Terbium and yttrium are heavy rare earth elements — the highest-value REE categories — with no current North American or allied-nation mine producing them at scale. For junior REE investors benchmarking exploration-stage cash burn against discovery quality, $3.5M in H1 operating spend to advance a heavy REE discovery in a stable Brazilian jurisdiction represents efficient capital deployment.

headline: EAGLE PLAINS AND KESTREL GOLD SIGN MPW LOI — BC Grab Returns 161 g/t Ag and 8.4% Cu at New Silver-Copper Target
snippet: Eagle Plains Resources (TSX-V: EPL) signed a letter of intent with Kestrel Gold to option the MPW Project in British Columbia, with a new mineralized occurrence confirmed by grab samples returning 161 g/t Ag and 8.4% Cu at the new target. The deal transfers exploration risk to Kestrel while giving Eagle Plains a royalty or carried interest on future success. Silver at 161 g/t with copper at 8.4% from surface grab samples is a compelling polymetallic starting point in BC's well-established permitting environment.

headline: METALSOURCE SILVER HILL OPENS 17.28M ZONE SOUTH OF HIGH-GRADE — New Intercept Confirms System Has Two-Direction Growth Potential
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) reported that drill hole SH26-27 intercepted a 17.28-metre zone of silver-equivalent mineralization at the Silver Hill project, south of the company's previously identified high-grade intervals, confirming the system is open to the south. The result demonstrates that Silver Hill is not a single high-grade shoot but a laterally extensive mineralized system — a critical distinction for resource estimation potential. Assay results are pending, but the width of the mineralized interval is itself significant for a junior silver explorer.

headline: URANIUM MINERS DOWN 23% WHILE SPOT HOLDS $91.55/LB — Equity-Price Gap Widens; Analyst Flags Financing Risk vs. Structural Physical Demand
snippet: An analysis from Discovery Alert documents the widening divergence between uranium equity performance and spot uranium prices: miners are down approximately 23% year-to-date in 2026 while spot uranium sits near US$91.55/lb and term contracts hold at US$98.00/lb. The analyst attributes the dislocation to investor concern about financing and execution risk at development-stage uranium companies — not to any weakness in underlying demand, which remains underpinned by new nuclear builds and utility re-contracting. The piece argues the disconnect is historically unusual and suggests investors distinguish between operators with contracted revenue streams and pure explorers exposed to capital market conditions.

headline: ENERGY FUELS TARGETS 1.6-2M LBS OF U3O8 IN 2026 — US Uranium Production Rebuilds; Company Guides 35% Sales Growth for 2027
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU / TSX: EFR) is rebuilding domestic US uranium production after restarting mining in late 2023, with approximately 1.6 million to 2 million pounds of mined and produced uranium expected in 2026 and sales projected to increase approximately 35% in 2027 as new utility contracts come into effect. As the only US producer of both uranium and rare earth elements, Energy Fuels occupies a rare strategic position in domestic critical minerals supply. The 2026 production range confirms the restart is proceeding on schedule and sets up a meaningful step-change in revenue for the fiscal year ahead.

headline: GOLD MINERS AT HISTORICALLY CHEAP VALUATIONS AGAINST ALL-TIME EARNINGS — Smaller Producers Just Logged One of Their Best Quarters Ever
snippet: An Investing.com analysis argues that smaller gold mining companies have simultaneously delivered one of their best-ever quarterly earnings periods while reaching record-low valuation multiples relative to those earnings — a historically unusual combination that has preceded sustained re-ratings in prior cycles. The piece warns the case could stall if Q4 2026 average gold prices fall materially from their current range, as a weaker quarterly average would compress reported earnings even if physical gold remains above $3,500. The gap between operational performance and stock prices is the central case for counter-trend accumulation into the November correction.

headline: FCX BEAR SIGNAL AFTER 7.8% BOUNCE — Schaeffer's: Only 20% Chance Higher a Month Later After This Pattern; 18 of 24 Analysts Still Rate Buy
snippet: Schaeffer's quantitative analysis identified a fresh bear signal on Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) after the stock rallied 7.8% to approximately $49.59, finding that FCX was higher one month later in only 20% of historical cases following similar setups. The finding contradicts consensus: 18 of 24 brokerage analysts rate FCX a buy or strong buy — a bullish wall of analyst opinion that Schaeffer's argues has historically been a contrary indicator at inflection points. For retail investors tempted to buy copper miners into the November rebound, the signal suggests the bounce may be relief rather than reversal.

headline: FTSE 100 MINING STOCKS FALL AHEAD OF PCE — Rio Tinto, BHP, Anglo American Drag Index as Global Investors Position Before Wednesday US Inflation Data
snippet: FTSE 100-listed mining majors including Rio Tinto, BHP and Anglo American pulled the index lower on November 24 as global investors reduced risk positions ahead of Wednesday's US PCE inflation release — the last liquid macro catalyst before the Thanksgiving holiday closes US markets. The London session selloff reflects the same caution visible in US markets: a hot PCE read revives near-certain pricing for a December 50bps Fed hike and would erase much of Monday's recovery across metals equities worldwide. For TSX-V junior investors, FTSE miner weakness signals that institutional selling pressure in the sector is synchronized globally, not a North American-specific phenomenon.
